verdict.rationale: OpenClaw is self-hosted on the user's own machine. It stores agent memory as plain Markdown files in the local workspace and keeps session history in SQLite, so the data sits on the user's disk in open formats they can take with them. However, no documented export command, bulk-export feature or migration-out guide is evidenced. Missing for 10: a first-party export/backup tool covering all data (memory, sessions, config, skills, automations), documentation on leaving or migrating out, and independent or hands-on confirmation of data portability.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: OpenClaw remembers things by writing plain Markdown files in your agent's workspace
each with its own workspace, state directory (`agentDir`), and SQLite-backed session history
Run one Gateway process on your own machine and message your AI assistant from anywhere.
